why: Checks 1 and 2 test only what their lines say: padding with fill, a space by default, and returning s unchanged when it is already long enough. Check 4 asks only for exit 0 and fail 0. Check 3 is stricter than its line. The line only says README.md "has a section for every function index.js exports". The FAIL condition, though, needs a heading at level ## or deeper whose text starts with the function name, optionally in backticks (regex `^#{2,}\s+`?name\b`). A real section such as "## Padding strings with padLeft" or "# padLeft" would print MISSING and fail. The words don't require any heading level or wording, so this exact-wording rule should be under Advisory, not in PASS/FAIL. The check also says to look at slugify "closely", which is fine, but the heading-format rule alone breaks the criterion.
